thesis_read: This stretch the company made its first genuine per-customer commercial decision: the value arm priced 263 accounts individually on expected value, and the world gained the ability to punish it for getting that wrong -- until yesterday a supplier 200% above the market lost the same third of its book as one 25% above, so a flat-rules baseline could be neither beaten nor lost to. Against the thesis that is real movement, and the belief-vs-truth gap on price moving from -7.8pp to +0.5pp is the wall doing exactly what it exists to do. But the honest read is that an inference advantage still cannot be claimed, for two separate reasons and neither is small. The two organs the advantage must come from both measure WORSE than no-skill: the CLV estimator carries 1.76x the error of simply assigning every account the population mean, and the win-rate learning loop is at 1.23x never updating at all -- the company's belief about itself is currently anti-informative. So: the machinery of per-customer decision exists, the instrument that would tell us it works does not yet mean anything, and it reports `fit_to_run: false` on itself. Not backwards -- five atoms self-certified to L2 and the price cap, the journal sign and 6,747 phantom drawdowns were all genuinely fixed -- but the project is closer to the thesis in machinery than in evidence. Two things are drifting. The director named the 117 H_harness atoms twice on 24 August, once at 20:45 and again at 21:24 ("the map should be half the size and true"); it is still exactly 117 and nothing has read them. And publishing has been down 11.8 hours with the publish commit refusing to land on 12 consecutive episodes against a green scoped suite, so the carbon figure he called the entire point of this project is stale on the live surface.

thesis_read: Three hours, eleven commits, nine substantive, and the top of the last record was answered properly: the value arm no longer reports a ceiling as a decision. A coarse grid that could only ever return one of its own sixteen numbers now brackets, and a refinement decides -- 107 accounts sitting on exactly GBP 130 became a concentration of 1.9%, with interior optima on 257 of 263 and only one account still at the top of its grid. That is the difference between a per-customer decision and a rule wearing one, and it is the single most thesis-relevant thing this project has built. LANE 0 landed too, so this record is reachable by a draw, and publishing is live again -- the cause was never the deadline but two files git had never seen, and the receipt redesign the last record ordered was correctly REJECTED on analysis rather than built, because only the second gate can see what the commit is landing. Both of those items therefore leave focus. What the improved arm bought is a much sharper problem, and it is the world's, not the company's. Freed to choose, the arm chose a median of GBP 115/MWh and a +53% median bill -- roughly GBP 900 a year on a typical account -- and it is right to, because `simulation/market_switching_propensity.py:55` caps the world's annual switching rate at 22% once savings available pass GBP 400, and both sides cap the leave probability at 0.95. So the world models one in five leaving whether a rival is GBP 400 or GBP 2,000 cheaper, and one in twenty staying whatever they are charged. The arm has priced its entire book into the flat top of that curve, which is beyond anything the DESNZ series it was fitted to ever observed. This is the coupled-triad rule biting exactly where it was meant to: no company capability is complete until it has faced a world that can defeat it, and this world cannot defeat a supplier that gouges. It also weakens the headline comparison -- a +2.0pp belief-versus-truth gap between an estimator and a truth fitted from the same published series, read where neither has data, is co-calibration and not demonstrated inference. So the honest position is that the per-customer machinery is now real and the instrument that would judge it is not. On the previous focus: the brief again reports none of it drawn, and again the brief is wrong -- it counts maturity-map atom draws only, and three of the five items were non-atom instructions, two of which landed.
